facts.statement: The genus Mesadactylus was named in 1989 by James Jensen and Kevin Padian.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1989 by James Jensen and Kevin Padian.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Mesadactylus ornithosphyos.
facts.quote: The type species is Mesadactylus ornithosphyos.

facts.statement: Mesadactylus is an extinct pterosaur genus found in the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Colorado, United States.
facts.quote: Mesadactylus ('mesa finger') is an extinct genus of pterosaur from the Kimmeridgian-Tithonian-age Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Colorado, United States.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, BYU 2024, consists of a synsacrum made of seven fused sacral vertebrae with a unique complete fusion of spinae into a supraneural blade.
facts.quote: The holotype is BYU 2024, a synsacrum of seven sacral vertebrae, featuring a unique—for a pterosaur—complete fusion of the spinae into a supraneural blade

facts.statement: Associated remains include arm bones, pectoral girdle bones, vertebrae, and femora.
facts.quote: Further referred associated remains include arms bones, pectoral girdle bones, vertebrae (including cervix and sacral), and femora.

facts.statement: Additional material, including a partial braincase, was described in 2004 and 2006.
facts.quote: Additional material was described in 2004 (including a partial braincase) and 2006

facts.statement: In 2007, S. Christopher Bennett claimed that the holotype and referred material came from different forms, arguing the synsacrum belonged to an Anurognathidae member while the rest was pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: In 2007 S. Christopher Bennett claimed that the holotype and the referred material came from different forms and that, while the last was indeed of a pterodactyloid nature, the synsacrum belonged to a member of the Anurognathidae.

facts.statement: Jensen and Padian originally classified Mesadactylus as a pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: Jensen and Padian classified Mesadactylus as a pterodactyloid.

facts.statement: Mesadactylus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, between 152.21 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some sources question whether Mesadactylus belongs to the family Anurognathidae.

rejected.statement: In 2006, the authors suggested that the larger contemporary Kepodactylus might be the same animal as Mesadactylus, despite minor differences.
rejected.quote: in the latter publication, the authors suggested that its larger contemporary Kepodactylus could be the same animal, although there are minor differences.
